# Start here {.unnumbered}

This book is the **recipe** for the TrainStat model that is built on Days 4 to 7 of the boot camp. It is written so that a facilitator, a participant, a reviewer or another AI assistant can rebuild every sheet, check every number and choose a different path where the course path does not suit. It has four layers.

1. **Specification.** Every sheet, every row, every formula in the first timeline column, taken directly from the verified workbooks (not retyped).
2. **Prompts.** For each of the 24 build blocks, five ready-to-paste prompts: a tutor, a formula generator, a script builder, an independent replica and an auditor. Each prompt contains the specification, the input values and the checkpoints, so it works on its own.
3. **Evidence.** Every checkpoint number was produced by an independent engine and agrees with Microsoft Excel (the final build was recalculated in Excel for Mac on 10 October 2026 in all three scenarios) and with a full formula evaluation of the delivered workbooks. Base case: shareholder NPV **17,609.0**, XIRR **33.72%** (start model); sized debt **72,154.2** at gearing **71.39%**, minimum DSCR **2.2966x**, blended sponsor IRR **43.03% measured from COD** (**34.71%** when each contribution is dated when it is paid; see the retained conventions) (project-finance model).
4. **Options.** Alternative paths (drawdown, interest during construction, repayment style, DSRA, shareholder loan, tax treatment, sizing) with the effect of each on the answer, computed, not guessed.

::: {.callout-tip title="The interactive companion"}
`mipf_model_builder.html` (same folder) runs the whole model in your browser. Change any input, switch any option, see every statement, ratio, check and chart, and export the prompts tailored to **your** inputs, with the expected results for those inputs inserted in the checkpoints. Use it to explore; use this book to build.
:::

## How to use this book {.unnumbered}

| If you want to... | Do this |
|---|---|
| Learn to build the model in Excel | Pick **Path A** (tutor) and work through blocks B00 to B23 in order. Paste the tutor prompt, then type the formulas yourself. |
| Build quickly and correct later | Pick **Path B** (formula generator), paste, fill right, then run **V** (verify) before moving on. |
| Rebuild the workbook reproducibly | Pick **Path C** (script). Keep the generated scripts in version control. |
| Prove that a workbook is right | Pick **Path D** (replica) and compare to the precision shown (the Atlas holds full-precision values), then run **V**. |
| Change the structure (e.g. equity first, no DSRA) | Go to the **Options** table at the end of the block and to the [options atlas](#sec-options); each option says what to change in the prompt and what the answer becomes. |
| Read and challenge the model without building it | Pick **Path L** (see the chapter on scope, caveats and retained conventions) and answer the ten credit questions in the app. |
| Teach it | Use the Day 4 to Day 7 slide decks for the sessions and this book for homework and self-study. |

# The build paths {#sec-paths}

| Path | What happens | Best for | Cost / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Manual build in Excel, guided by an AI tutor** | You type every formula yourself and the assistant only coaches. Best for learning and for the live classroom; slowest; the highest retention. | Learners, facilitators | Time x4 vs C; no code needed |
| **B. Paste-ready formulas from an AI (Copilot or chat)** | The assistant returns the exact formula for each row (first timeline column and constant column) with keystrokes; you paste and fill right. | Practitioners who know Excel but not this model | Fast; the risk is copying without understanding, so always run the verify prompt |
| **C. Script that writes the workbook (Python openpyxl)** | The assistant writes a function that creates the sheet with formulas as text. Fully reproducible, version-controlled and testable; this is how the delivered model was built. | Modellers who need many variants or an audit trail | Needs Python; remember the _xlfn. prefix for MINIFS and other new functions |
| **D. Independent replica (Python or JavaScript)** | The assistant re-implements the block as plain code. Used to prove the spreadsheet is right: two independent builds that agree to the precision of the checkpoints are strong evidence. | Reviewers, model auditors | Catches wiring errors that checks cannot see |
| **V. Audit and diff against the specification** | The assistant compares a dump of your sheet with the specification and the checkpoints and lists every deviation. | Everyone, after every block | Cheapest quality gate; never skip |
| **L. Lender and lawyer reading path** | No Excel build: run the interactive app and answer ten credit questions (see Scope, caveats and retained conventions). | Lawyers, credit officers, regulators | Fast; you learn to read the model, not to build it |

**Rule of thumb.** Never move to the next block until the verify prompt (V) returns PASS and the checkpoints agree. Errors compound across sheets; a wrong flag in `Time` poisons everything.

# Scope, caveats and retained conventions {#sec-caveats}

Read this chapter before using any number in the book for anything other than learning. The case is a teaching case.

::: {.callout-warning title="Illustrative teaching case"}
The inputs (US$ fares, a 6.5% all-in US$ debt rate, inflation falling from 7% to 3%, a 2.25x target DSCR, a 25.25% required return) are not calibrated to any market. Nothing in this book or the app is investment, legal, tax or credit advice. The credit agreement, the concession and the applicable tax law govern a real transaction; covenant levels quoted are examples.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="One currency"}
All amounts are in US$ thousands and revenue is effectively treated as US$ or fully FX-indexed. A Nigerian passenger-rail project would earn naira fares that are often politically set and pay US$ debt: the currency mismatch, indexation lag and convertibility/transfer risk are a lender's first questions. Mitigants to study: local-currency tranches (for example guaranteed local bonds), hedging, political-risk or partial-risk cover (for example MIGA, a partial risk guarantee, ATI), and fare indexation to FX. The model contains none of these. The inflation path (7% to 3%) is a US$ path.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Tax is jurisdiction-specific"}
The model uses a 30% corporate tax rate, tax depreciation of 5% of the written-down value per quarter (about 18.5% a year), full deductibility of senior and shareholder-loan interest, and cash refunds of tax losses. In Nigeria verify the current rules (the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and its commencement): the corporate rate and any development levy or minimum effective tax, capital-allowance rules and restrictions, loss relief (carry-forward, not refund), limits on interest paid to foreign connected persons (a cap by reference to EBITDA with carry-forward of the excess), transfer-pricing rules for the shareholder-loan rate, withholding tax on interest and dividends and treaty relief, and any sector incentives.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Shareholder loans"}
Interest on a shareholder loan is deductible only within interest-limitation rules and at an arm's-length rate; payments are restricted payments under the credit agreement (same lock-up and distribution conditions as dividends); withholding tax applies. A structure with all sponsor funding as loan and no share capital is not permitted by company law or lenders.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Sizing versus covenants"}
Debt is sized once, on the lender's case (for demand-risk rail often a P90 traffic case; in this course the Base case plays that role, and a real lender's own P90 case would normally support less than the 72,154 shown), and the other scenarios then test that fixed structure. The book therefore shows both the re-solved scenarios (useful for structuring) and the Downside and breakeven cases on the FIXED financing (what a credit committee reads). Sizing DSCRs differ from covenant levels: lock-up about 1.10x to 1.20x and default about 1.00x to 1.10x, tested at each calculation date on a historic (and often also a projected) 12-month basis; LLCR tests use the projections.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="What this model leaves out"}
Construction contingency, development and advisory fees, initial DSRA funding in the uses, a major-maintenance reserve account (rolling-stock overhauls), hedging, cash sweep, ramp-up, refinancing, an equity bridge, standby equity or a cost-overrun facility, change-in-law and compensation events, lock-up tests on dividends and shareholder-loan payments, a DSRA draw to cover a shortfall, tax-loss carry-forward (app option only), and timing of sponsor funding in the IRR (see R1).
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Confidentiality when using AI tools"}
Do not paste confidential client or transaction data into AI tools that your organisation has not approved. The prompts in this book use only the public teaching case.
:::

## Conventions retained from the original workbook {.unnumbered}

These are known simplifications. They were not changed so that every checkpoint matches the delivered workbook; each is quantified so that you can decide.

| # | Convention | What it does | Effect and option |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Retained convention: sponsor funding dated at COD | Val dates all sponsor funding at COD although equity is paid in during construction, so the blended IRR (43.03% Base) and the NPV are both measured from COD and overstate the return; they cannot rank drawdown options. | Not changed in the workbook; the app also reports the IRR dated at the construction quarters (34.71% Base; equity first 32.03%). |
| R2 | Retained convention: tax losses refunded | Negative taxable income produces a cash tax refund in the same quarter (4 quarters in Base, 11 in Downside). | Not changed; app option to carry losses forward (Downside minimum DSCR 2.34x to 2.25x). |

## Path L: the lender and lawyer reading path (no Excel build) {.unnumbered}

Use the interactive app and this book without building the model. Run the Base case, then answer these ten credit questions with the app (tabs Summary, Debt and cover, Scenarios and sensitivity, Prompt studio).

1. What are the quarterly and the rolling 12-month minimum DSCR on the fixed Base financing under the Downside, and in which quarter does the weakest one occur? (Scenarios and sensitivity tab, 'financing fixed'.)
2. How far can the fare fall before the minimum DSCR reaches 1.20x (lock-up) and 1.00x (default)? (Breakeven line.)
3. Which constraint sets the debt size in each scenario, DSCR or the gearing cap, and what does that tell you about who bears the risk?
4. What happens to the sponsor IRR if the DSRA is 4 quarters instead of 2? Is the lender's comfort worth it to the sponsor?
5. Why is the blended IRR measured from COD higher than the IRR dated at the contribution dates, and which would you show a credit committee?
6. What does the equity-first drawdown do to total project cost, and why do lenders usually prefer it?
7. Which contract clause controls each of the three largest inputs (fare, occupancy, hard cost)? (Contract map.)
8. Where does the model assume a protection that a real credit agreement would have to provide (DSRA funding at COD, lock-up, DSRA draw)?
9. What would a currency mismatch do to the Downside? Which risks in this model would you transfer, insure or hedge?
10. Which three results would you ask the sponsor to re-run with their own downside before approving the structure?

# The model charter {#sec-charter}

Paste this charter at the start of any conversation, or let each block prompt carry it (they do). It is the contract that makes the formulas auditable.

::: {.prompt}
```text
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).
```
:::

# Prompt patterns that work for modelling {#sec-patterns}

| Pattern | How | In this book |
|---|---|---|
| Spec first, code second | Ask for the specification (rows, formulas, checkpoints) before any formula or code. Review it. Only then ask for the build. | Prompts in this book always contain the spec table, so a model cannot invent the structure. |
| Checkpoint-driven | Give the expected numbers and ask the assistant to state which checkpoint each step is meant to hit. | Every block ends with checkpoint values computed by an independent engine. |
| One block per conversation turn | Build one sheet at a time and verify before the next. | Errors compound across sheets; a wrong flag in Time poisons everything. |
| Two independent builds | Build the same block with different tools (Excel vs Python) and compare to the precision of the checkpoints. | This is how the delivered model was verified: Excel, Python and JavaScript agree. |
| Red-team the answer | After a build, ask the assistant to find five ways the block could be wrong and to test each. | Use the Verify prompt; its checklist covers signs, units, ranges, flags and hard-codes. |
| Ask for assumptions, not just results | Require the assistant to list every assumption it makes (day count, sign, timing) in a table. | Hidden assumptions are the main source of silent differences. |
| Pin the tool facts | State the Excel version, OS and the functions allowed (no OFFSET, no volatile functions, MINIFS needs _xlfn. in scripts). | Prevents formulas that do not exist on the user's machine. |

# A worked tutor session (Path A) {#sec-transcript}

What a good Path A conversation looks like for block B05 (OpCost). The tutor explains, hints and checks; the learner types.

**You:** (paste the Path A prompt for B05, then) Start with the first pull row.

**Tutor:** Before the formula: row 11 pulls the handling cost per arrival from InpC into this sheet. Why do we pull it first instead of typing =InpC!F44 inside the calculation row? (Hint: think about who will audit this sheet.)

**You:** So the calculation row only has references on the same sheet, and anyone can see the driver.

**Tutor:** Yes. Type it in cell F11, then tell me what you typed. Windows: Ctrl+G, F11, Enter, type, Enter. Mac: Ctrl+G, F11, Return.

**You:** =InpC!F$44

**Tutor:** Correct pattern: the row anchor $44 keeps the reference fixed if the cell is copied down. What value do you see in F11? The checkpoint is 550.

**You:** 550. Next row?

**Tutor:** Row 16 is the first calculation. In plain English: if this quarter is a forecast quarter, cost = cost per arrival / 1,000 x arrivals x escalation. Write the formula for J16; you have the pulled rows 11 to 15 above it.

**You:** =IF(J15=1,F11/F12\*J13\*J14,0)

**Tutor:** Almost: F11 and F12 must be anchored as $F11 and $F12 so the formula still points at column F when you fill right to CO. Fix it, fill J16:CO16 with Ctrl+Enter (Mac Ctrl+Return), then read H16 and L16. Checkpoints: H16 = 890,187 and L16 = 7,760.

# The build blocks {#sec-blocks}

Each block follows the same eleven-part pattern: purpose, concept, inputs, build order, specification, prompts (five paths), checkpoints, options, failure modes. Values shown are the course **Base** case unless stated.


## B00 Workbook standards and skeleton {#sec-b00}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 4 (Mon 19 Oct) · **Sheet(s)** workbook structure · **Depends on** Nothing · **Produces** Blank sheets Cover, Dashboard, InpC, InpS, Time, Esc, OpRev, OpCost, Tax, NCA, Debt, Equity, FinStat, Val, Track (PF adds Constr, Sculpt, DSRA, SHL, Ratios) · **Suggested time (Path A)** 20 minutes

**By the end you can** set up a workbook that any reviewer can navigate and check by pattern.
:::

**Purpose.** Create an empty, correctly wired workbook before any calculation: sheet order, layout columns, colour code, named ranges, calculation settings. Everything later depends on this skeleton.

**Concept.** A model is read far more often than it is written. Fixing the layout once lets every formula be audited by pattern: the same column means the same thing on every sheet, and a reviewer can check a row by looking at its first two cells.

### Build order

1. Create sheets in this order: Cover, Dashboard, InpC, InpS, Time, Esc, Constr, OpRev, OpCost, Tax, NCA, Debt, Sculpt, DSRA, SHL, Equity, FinStat, Ratios, Val, Track (Windows: Ctrl+Shift+F11 / Shift+F11 to insert; Mac: Fn+Shift+F11).
2. Suggested formatting: narrow columns A to D, a wide column E for labels, columns F to H for constant, unit and total, J to CO for the timeline; freeze panes at J6 (View > Freeze Panes) so labels and dates stay visible.
3. Colour code: yellow fill = typed input; blue font = pulled link; red font = result row. Define the styles once (Home > Cell Styles) and reuse.
4. Define names (Formulas > Name Manager; Ctrl+F3): CHK_TOL = InpC!$F$101, unit = InpC!$F$102, TRACK_ACTIVE = Track!$H$5, LIVE_RESULTS = Track!$H$8:$H$69, TRK_COMMENT = Track!$H$77:$H$78.
5. File > Options > Formulas: calculation Automatic; iterative calculation OFF (a circular reference must be a visible error, not silently iterated).
6. Save as MIPF_TrainStat_v00.xlsx and keep a numbered copy after every block (v01, v02 ...).

::: {.panel-tabset}

MODEL CHARTER (applies to every row)
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.

4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.

HOW YOU MUST TEACH

### Checkpoints

- Twenty sheets in the stated order; no sheet hidden
- Name Manager shows five names, none with #REF!
- Calculation mode Automatic; iterative calculation off

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Fewer sheets | Merge Sculpt, DSRA, SHL and Ratios into one 'Debt' sheet. | Shorter navigation but a longer sheet; auditing by sheet purpose is harder. The prompts still work: change the sheet name in each prompt. |
| Semi-annual model | Months per model period = 6 and 42 columns. | The engine and the specification assume 84 quarterly columns; every period count (tenor 40, DSRA 2) changes meaning. Re-derive the checkpoints. |
| Different currency or unit | Change the unit label and InpC row 102. | Only labels change; nothing else depends on the unit except the 1/1000 conversion in OpCost. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| #REF! in a name | A name points at a deleted cell | Rebuild the name; never delete rows that names point to |
| Model slow to recalculate | Formulas or formats extend to column XFD | Delete columns beyond CO (the original file carried about 1.2 million ghost cells) |
| Results do not change after switching the scenario | Calculation mode is Manual (the original file was saved that way) | Formulas > Calculation Options > Automatic; press F9 once |
| Circular reference warning | Iterative calculation was switched on to hide a loop | Switch it off and fix the loop algebraically (see B14) |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why switch iterative calculation off?
   *Answer:* Because a circular reference must be a visible error. Iteration silently hides loops that should be removed algebraically.
2. Why one formula per row?
   *Answer:* So a reviewer can check a row by its first two cells and any difference across the row is a defect, not a design choice.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: #REF! in a name. *Likely cause and fix:* A name points at a deleted cell. Rebuild the name; never delete rows that names point to.
2. You see: Model slow to recalculate. *Likely cause and fix:* Formulas or formats extend to column XFD. Delete columns beyond CO (the original file carried about 1.2 million ghost cells).
3. You see: Results do not change after switching the scenario. *Likely cause and fix:* Calculation mode is Manual (the original file was saved that way). Formulas > Calculation Options > Automatic; press F9 once.
4. You see: Circular reference warning. *Likely cause and fix:* Iterative calculation was switched on to hide a loop. Switch it off and fix the loop algebraically (see B14).
:::


## B01 Inputs: constants by scenario (InpC) and time series (InpS) {#sec-b01}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 4 · **Sheet(s)** InpC, InpS · **Depends on** B00 · **Produces** Column F of InpC (active constants); rows of InpS used by OpRev, OpCost and Debt · **Suggested time (Path A)** 40 minutes

**By the end you can** drive the whole model from one scenario switch and two input sheets.
:::

**Purpose.** Hold every assumption in two places only: scalar constants per scenario (InpC) and quarterly time series (InpS). The scenario selector lets one switch drive the whole model.

**Concept.** Scenario columns J, K, L hold Base, Downside and Upside values; column F picks the active one with =INDEX(I:M,$F$4), where F4 = MATCH(F3,I3:M3,0). Changing only F3 re-runs the entire model. The corrected scenario definitions are: Base (inflation 7% falling to 3%, fare 7.15), Downside (fare -10% = 6.435 and O&M +10%), Upside (fare +10% = 7.865). In the original file Upside was worse than Base and Downside equalled Base; both were fixed. Currency: every amount is in one currency (US$ thousands). Revenue is therefore treated as US$ or fully FX-indexed. A real Nigerian project with naira fares and US$ debt needs a currency-mismatch analysis (see the caveats chapter) that this teaching model does not contain.

### Build order

1. On InpC write the scenario names in J3:L3 (Base, Downside, Upside); put the active name in F3 with a drop-down (Data > Data Validation > List =$J$3:$L$3).
2. F4: =MATCH(F3,I3:M3,0).
3. For each input row type the label (E), unit (G) and the three scenario values (J:L, yellow). Then in F type =INDEX(I{r}:M{r},$F$4) and copy down (Ctrl+D). Use Ctrl+Shift+Enter in pre-365 Excel if you see braces in the original.
4. Rows 17 to 21: inflation by inflation year (start dates in E). Rows 56 to 62: capex by date (E).
5. InpS: time series across J:CO: trains (rows 8, 9), arrivals per train (11, 12), occupancy (14, 15), repayment profiles 1 to 3 (18 to 20, totals 100%), additional debt and equity (22, 23).
6. Name the tolerance (row 101) CHK_TOL and the unit (row 102) 'unit'.

```text
ROLE
You are a patient Excel modelling tutor on the Mastering Infrastructure and Project Finance Boot Camp (Lagos Business School). You coach; you do not do the work for me.

TASK
I am building this block of the TrainStat project-finance model in Excel on Windows or Mac: Inputs: constants by scenario (InpC) and time series (InpS) (sheet or sheets: InpC, InpS).
Purpose: Hold every assumption in two places only: scalar constants per scenario (InpC) and quarterly time series (InpS). The scenario selector lets one switch drive the whole model.
Prerequisites already built and passing their checks: B00
What this block must deliver: Column F of InpC (active constants); rows of InpS used by OpRev, OpCost and Debt

MODEL CHARTER (applies to every row)
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

```text
ROLE
You are an Excel formula generator for a quarterly project-finance model. You output exact, paste-ready formulas and nothing speculative.

TASK
Produce every formula needed for this block of the TrainStat model: Inputs: constants by scenario (InpC) and time series (InpS) (sheet or sheets: InpC, InpS). Excel version: Microsoft 365 or 2019 on Windows or Mac. Allowed functions: only those that appear in the specification of the model, namely ABS, AND, AVERAGEIFS, DATE, DAY, EOMONTH, IF, IFNA, INDEX, MATCH, MAX, MIN, MINIFS, MONTH, SUM, SUMIFS, SUMPRODUCT, TEXT, VLOOKUP, XIRR, YEAR, FORMULATEXT. Forbidden: OFFSET, INDIRECT, volatile functions, macros, circular references, iterative calculation.
Purpose: Hold every assumption in two places only: scalar constants per scenario (InpC) and quarterly time series (InpS). The scenario selector lets one switch drive the whole model.

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

#### C Script

::: {.prompt}
```text
ROLE
You are a senior Python engineer who builds auditable Excel models with openpyxl.

TASK
Write a function build_sheet(wb, spec) that creates or completes this block in an openpyxl workbook: Inputs: constants by scenario (InpC) and time series (InpS) (sheet or sheets: InpC, InpS) using exactly the specification below. Return a list of (cell, expected_value, tolerance) checks so that I can test the workbook after recalculation in Excel.
Purpose: Hold every assumption in two places only: scalar constants per scenario (InpC) and quarterly time series (InpS). The scenario selector lets one switch drive the whole model.

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

TOOL FACTS
openpyxl 3.1 writes formulas as text and never calculates them; recalculation happens in Excel. Use _xlfn. for MINIFS, XLOOKUP and similar. Avoid array formulas; where the course workbook shows braces use a plain INDEX formula. Keep the workbook under 1 MB: never touch cells beyond column CO.

ROLE
You are a quantitative developer building an independent replica of a spreadsheet block to prove it is right.

TASK
Re-implement this block as plain code in Python 3 (standard library only) or JavaScript (ES2020, no dependencies): Inputs: constants by scenario (InpC) and time series (InpS) (sheet or sheets: InpC, InpS). The replica must not read the workbook: it takes the inputs below and returns the named rows as arrays over 84 quarterly columns (index 0 = 30 Sep 2021, index 1 = COD 31 Dec 2021). The one exception is Constr, which has 8 columns from the quarter ending 31 Mar 2020 to COD.
Purpose: Hold every assumption in two places only: scalar constants per scenario (InpC) and quarterly time series (InpS). The scenario selector lets one switch drive the whole model.
How the block works: Scenario columns J, K, L hold Base, Downside and Upside values; column F picks the active one with =INDEX(I:M,$F$4), where F4 = MATCH(F3,I3:M3,0). Changing only F3 re-runs the entire model. The corrected scenario definitions are: Base (inflation 7% falling to 3%, fare 7.15), Downside (fare -10% = 6.435 and O&M +10%), Upside (fare +10% = 7.865). In the original file Upside was worse than Base and Downside equalled Base; both were fixed. Currency: every amount is in one currency (US$ thousands). ROLE

I will paste a dump of the sheet: for each row the label, column F, the formulas in J, K and L (as typed), the total in H and the value in L. (How to make the dump: in a spare column type =FORMULATEXT(J11) and fill down the rows, or press Ctrl+` and copy the sheet, plus a values copy of columns E, F, H and L. The charter below lists the documented exceptions; do not report them as faults.)

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).

### Checkpoints

- Switching F3 between the three names changes F35 (fare) to 7.15, 6.435 and 7.865
- InpS H18:H20 sum to 100% (profile totals)
- InpC J46 = 0, K46 = 10%, L46 = 0 (live O&M sensitivity)

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Scenario count | Add a fourth scenario column M. | Extend the MATCH range and every INDEX; nothing else changes. |
| Sensitivity inputs instead of scenarios | Keep one case and add X% shock inputs (fare, O&M, occupancy). | Faster for tornado charts; loses the coherent story that a scenario gives. |
| Data validation vs. typed names | Use a drop-down on F3. | Prevents #N/A from a mistyped scenario name; recommended. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| #N/A in column F | Scenario name in F3 not found in J3:L3 | Use the drop-down |
| Upside worse than Base | Original file defined Upside with 2% flat inflation | Use the corrected inputs |
| Profile does not sum to 100% | Typed percentages rounded | Make the last quarter = 1 - SUM(previous) |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. What do the J, K and L columns of InpC hold and what is in F?
   *Answer:* J, K and L hold the Base, Downside and Upside values; F holds the active value =INDEX(I:M,$F$4) picked by the scenario switch.
2. Why not type the fare inside the revenue formula?
   *Answer:* A typed number hides an assumption, cannot be changed by scenario and cannot be found by an audit of the inputs sheet.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: #N/A in column F. *Likely cause and fix:* Scenario name in F3 not found in J3:L3. Use the drop-down.
2. You see: Upside worse than Base. *Likely cause and fix:* Original file defined Upside with 2% flat inflation. Use the corrected inputs.
3. You see: Profile does not sum to 100%. *Likely cause and fix:* Typed percentages rounded. Make the last quarter = 1 - SUM(previous).
:::


## B02 Time sheet: calendar, flags and counters {#sec-b02}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 4 · **Sheet(s)** Time · **Depends on** B01 · **Produces** Rows 25 (period end), 30 (days), 37 (financial year), 45 (acquisition flag), 69 (forecast flag), 75 (last forecast flag), 95 (depreciation flag), 111 (phase label) · **Suggested time (Path A)** 40 minutes

**By the end you can** build the calendar and the 1/0 flags every other sheet multiplies by.
:::

**Purpose.** Create the 84-column timeline and every flag that other sheets multiply by: acquisition date, forecast period, last forecast period, depreciation period, days in period.

**Concept.** Flags are 1/0 switches (1 inside the period they describe). Multiplying by a flag is clearer and more auditable than nesting IF statements inside every calculation. The forecast starts the quarter after the acquisition date (31 Dec 2021) and lasts 20 years: 80 quarterly columns, so Time!H69 = 80. Day count corrected: the original file computed days in period as period ending less period beginning, where the beginning is the first day of the month, so a quarter showed 89 or 90 days instead of 90 or 91 (a 361-day year) while Constr used true days. The corrected workbook adds the missing day (Time row 30 = end - beginning + 1). Effect against the original: Base senior debt 72,403 to 72,154, blended IRR 43.34% to 43.03%, start-model NPV 17,688 to 17,609 (the app option 'original day count' reproduces the old numbers).

### Inputs used

| Input | Where | Base | Downside | Upside | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First date of time rulers | InpC row 9 | 2021-07-01 | 2021-07-01 | 2021-07-01 | date |
| Acquisition / initial balance date | InpC row 10 | 2021-12-31 | 2021-12-31 | 2021-12-31 | date |
| Length of forecast period | InpC row 11 | 20 | 20 | 20 | years |
| Months per model period | InpC row 12 | 3 | 3 | 3 | months |
| Useful life of NCA at acquisition | InpC row 65 | 15 | 15 | 15 | years |


### Build order

1. Period beginning (row 20): the first column takes the first date from InpC (F17); every later column is the first of the month after the previous period (DATE(YEAR(I20),MONTH(I20)+$F18,DAY(1))). Rows 24 and 29 pull it.
2. Period ending (row 25): =DATE(YEAR(J24),MONTH(J24)+$F23,DAY(J24)-1), i.e. the last day of the period. Days in period (row 30) = period ending (row 28) less period beginning (row 29) plus 1 (true calendar days; the original file omitted the +1).
3. Financial year (row 37) rolls forward when the period end passes the financial year end month (row 34).
4. Acquisition flag (row 45): =IF(J44=$F43,1,0). First forecast flag (row 53), pre-forecast flag (row 58), forecast flag (row 69): =IF(AND(J68>$F66,J68<=$F67),1,0), last forecast flag (row 75; the first column is typed 0), post-forecast flags (rows 79 and 83), depreciation flag (row 95).
5. Timeline label (row 111): a counter (row 104) that steps up at each phase flag, then =INDEX($F106:$F109,J110) picks Pre-fcst, Fin close, Forecast or Post-fcst from InpC rows 106 to 109.
6. Checks (rows 116 to 120): the column count (84) must equal pre-forecast + forecast + post-forecast totals; F120 = 0 when it does.

MODEL CHARTER (applies to every row)
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).

Forbidden: OFFSET, INDIRECT, volatile functions, macros, circular references, iterative calculation.
Purpose: Create the 84-column timeline and every flag that other sheets multiply by: acquisition date, forecast period, last forecast period, depreciation period, days in period.

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. How the block works: Flags are 1/0 switches (1 inside the period they describe). Multiplying by a flag is clearer and more auditable than nesting IF statements inside every calculation. The forecast starts the quarter after the acquisition date (31 Dec 2021) and lasts 20 years: 80 quarterly columns, so Time!H69 = 80. Day count corrected: the original file computed days in period as period ending less period beginning, where the beginning is the first day of the month, so a quarter showed 89 or 90 days instead of 90 or 91 (a 361-day year) while Constr used true days. The corrected workbook adds the missing day (Time row 30 = end - beginning + 1). Effect against the original: Base senior debt 72,403 to 72,154, blended IRR 43.34% to 43.03%, start-model NPV 17,688 to 17,609 (the app option 'original day count' reproduces the old numbers).

### Checkpoints

- Time!H45 = 1 (one acquisition column)
- Time!H69 = 80 forecast quarters
- Time!H75 = 1 (one last forecast quarter)
- Time!H95 = 60 depreciation quarters (15 years x 4)
- Time!F120 = 0 (modelling period check)
- Time!L25 = 31 Mar 2022 and L30 = 90 days (first forecast quarter; the original file showed 89)

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Fiscal year not ending in December | Change InpC row 98 (financial year end month). | Row 37 financial year labels shift; annual summaries on the Dashboard follow. |
| Monthly model | Months per period = 1; extend the ruler to 240+ columns. | All 'per quarter' constants (periods per year = 12) and the DSRA period count change; allow for slower recalculation. |
| Day-count basis | Use actual/365 instead of actual/360. | Change InpC row 79; Constr, Debt, Sculpt, SHL and Ratios pick it up automatically. |
| Original day count | Time!J30 = end - beginning (no +1). | Reproduces the original file (a 361-day year); not recommended: Time and Constr then disagree on the day count. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Flag sums wrong | Boundary condition > vs >= on the dates | Use > start and <= end exactly as in the spec |
| Last forecast flag never 1 | Equality test on dates that differ by a day | Compute the last date with EOMONTH, not by adding days |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why multiply by a flag instead of nesting IFs?
   *Answer:* A flag row is visible, checkable (its total must be 80, 60, 1) and reused by every sheet, so timing logic lives in one place.
2. Why is the acquisition column special?
   *Answer:* It is where opening balances are set to their initial values and where cumulative items restart.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: Flag sums wrong. *Likely cause and fix:* Boundary condition > vs >= on the dates. Use > start and <= end exactly as in the spec.
2. You see: Last forecast flag never 1. *Likely cause and fix:* Equality test on dates that differ by a day. Compute the last date with EOMONTH, not by adding days.
:::


## B03 Esc sheet: inflation and escalation factors {#sec-b03}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 4 · **Sheet(s)** Esc · **Depends on** B01, B02 · **Produces** Row 32 handling escalation factor; row 38 O&M escalation factor; CPI index row · **Suggested time (Path A)** 30 minutes

**By the end you can** turn annual inflation into escalation factors.
:::

**Purpose.** Convert annual inflation rates into quarterly indices and into the escalation factors that revenue, handling cost and O&M multiply by.

**Concept.** Quarterly inflation = (1 + annual rate)^(1/4) - 1, taken from the inflation year the quarter falls in (Base: 7% falling to 3%). The CPI index is 1 on the acquisition date and compounds quarterly. A contract signed when CPI was 120 (handling) or 132 (O&M) escalates by (CPI at acquisition / CPI at signature) x index.

### Inputs used

| Input | Where | Base | Downside | Upside | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPI index at acquisition date | InpC row 23 | 145 | 145 | 145 | index |
| CPI index at handling signature date | InpC row 25 | 120 | 120 | 120 | index |
| CPI index at O&M signature date | InpC row 27 | 132 | 132 | 132 | index |


### Build order

1. Pull the inflation table from InpC (rows 16 to 21) into Esc E10:F15 (start of each inflation year and its rate).
2. Annual rate for each quarter (row 17): =VLOOKUP(J16,$E11:$F15,2,TRUE): an approximate match on the period end date picks the rate of the inflation year the quarter falls in.
3. Periodic rate (row 21): =(1+J20)^(1/$F19)-1 where F19 = periods per year (4).
4. CPI escalation factor / index (row 26): =IF(J25=1,1,I26\*(1+J24)): 1 on the acquisition date, compounding quarterly after it (row 25 is the acquisition flag).
5. Handling escalation (row 32): =$F29/$F30\*J31 (CPI at acquisition / CPI at the handling contract date x index). O&M escalation (row 38): =$F35/$F36\*J37.

Purpose: Convert annual inflation rates into quarterly indices and into the escalation factors that revenue, handling cost and O&M multiply by.
How the block works: Quarterly inflation = (1 + annual rate)^(1/4) - 1, taken from the inflation year the quarter falls in (Base: 7% falling to 3%). ### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Contractual indexation | Use a fixed annual step (e.g. 3%) instead of CPI. | Replace the lookup row by a constant row; the factor rows are unchanged. |
| Currency mix | Split revenue into USD and local currency with different indices. | Add a second Esc block and a second revenue line; the structure is identical. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Index starts at 0 forever | Acquisition flag never 1 or compounding formula starts before the flag | Check Time!H45 = 1 first |
| Step jumps at the wrong quarter | Inflation-year start dates typed as 1 Mar but compared to quarter ends | Use the lookup on period end, as in the spec |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why compound the quarterly rate as (1+annual)^(1/4)-1?
   *Answer:* So four quarters compound to exactly the annual rate; dividing the annual rate by four would overstate inflation.
2. Why are handling and O&M escalated from different CPI dates?
   *Answer:* Each contract was signed when the index stood at a different level, so each escalates from its own base.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: Index starts at 0 forever. *Likely cause and fix:* Acquisition flag never 1 or compounding formula starts before the flag. Check Time!H45 = 1 first.
2. You see: Step jumps at the wrong quarter. *Likely cause and fix:* Inflation-year start dates typed as 1 Mar but compared to quarter ends. Use the lookup on period end, as in the spec.
:::


## B04 OpRev: arrivals, passengers, revenue and receivables {#sec-b04}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 4 · **Sheet(s)** OpRev · **Depends on** B01 to B03 · **Produces** Row 42 operating revenue (IS); row 54 revenue received (CF); row 65 receivables (BS) · **Suggested time (Path A)** 60 minutes

**By the end you can** build revenue from physical drivers and convert it to cash with a receivables roll-forward.
:::

**Purpose.** Build revenue from physical drivers (trains x arrivals x seats x occupancy x fare x escalation) and convert it to cash with a receivables roll-forward.

**Concept.** Revenue = fare x passengers / 1,000 x escalation (US$ thousands). Cash received in the quarter = opening receivables + the share of this quarter's revenue already paid: (days in period - receivable days) / days x revenue. Closing receivables = opening + revenue - cash received (the roll-forward identity). Receivables are zero on the acquisition date: the buyer starts clean.

### Inputs used

| Input | Where | Base | Downside | Upside | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Train capacity - domestic | InpC row 31 | 350 | 350 | 350 | seats |
| Train capacity - international | InpC row 33 | 150 | 150 | 150 | seats |
| Average fare per passenger | InpC row 35 | 7.15 | 6.435 | 7.865 | USD/pax |
| Account receivables days | InpC row 37 | 25 | 25 | 25 | days |
| CPI index at acquisition date | InpC row 23 | 145 | 145 | 145 | index |


### Build order

1. Pull trains (InpS rows 8 and 9, shown on OpRev rows 11 and 12), arrivals per train (rows 14 and 15) and the forecast flag (row 17).
2. Arrivals (rows 19 to 21): =IF(J$17=1,J11\*J14,0) domestic, the same for international, then the total.
3. Capacity (rows 23 and 24, seats per train from InpC) and occupancy (rows 26 and 27, from InpS). Passengers (rows 32 to 34): =$F23\*J26\*J29 domestic; =$F24\*J27\*J30 international; total = SUM.
4. Revenue (row 42): =IF(J41=1,$F37/$F38\*J39\*J40,0): fare / unit x passengers x CPI escalation factor (Esc row 26: fares follow CPI, costs follow contract-date escalation).
5. Cash from paid invoices (row 50): =(J48-$F47)/J48\*J49 (days in period less receivable days, over days). Revenue received (row 54) = SUM(J52:J53): opening receivables plus this quarter's cash.
6. Receivables (row 65): =IF(J60=1,$F59,J62+J63-J64): initial balance on the acquisition date, otherwise opening + revenue - cash received.

How the block works: Revenue = fare x passengers / 1,000 x escalation (US$ thousands). Cash received in the quarter = opening receivables + the share of this quarter's revenue already paid: (days in period - receivable days) / days x revenue. ROLE

TASK

The charter below lists the documented exceptions; do not report them as faults.)

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).

| Receivable days | Change InpC row 37 from 25 to 45. | Receivables rise; cash is received later; CFADS in the first years falls; revenue and IS do not change. |
| Demand shock | Use occupancy or trains multipliers. | Revenue is linear in fare and occupancy, so a -10% fare shock and a -10% occupancy shock give identical results (see the tornado). |
| Ramp-up | Add a ramp-up profile row on InpS and multiply passengers. | Delays the debt capacity; the sizing prompts in B16 pick it up automatically. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue stays 0 | Forecast flag not pulled (all zeros) | Check Time!J69 pull |
| Receivables negative | Signs reversed between received POS and CF row | POS rows positive, CF rows negative |
| Totals differ by a small factor | Unit (1,000) missing or doubled | Check the $F/$F pattern for the unit |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why does cash received lag revenue?
   *Answer:* Customers pay after the receivable days; the unpaid part is carried in receivables until it is collected.
2. What is the roll-forward identity?
   *Answer:* Closing receivables = opening + revenue - cash received.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: Revenue stays 0. *Likely cause and fix:* Forecast flag not pulled (all zeros). Check Time!J69 pull.
2. You see: Receivables negative. *Likely cause and fix:* Signs reversed between received POS and CF row. POS rows positive, CF rows negative.
3. You see: Totals differ by a small factor. *Likely cause and fix:* Unit (1,000) missing or doubled. Check the $F/$F pattern for the unit.
:::


## B05 OpCost: handling, O&M, payables {#sec-b05}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 4 · **Sheet(s)** OpCost · **Depends on** B01 to B04 · **Produces** Row 39 operating cost (IS); row 51 cost paid (CF); row 62 payables (BS) · **Suggested time (Path A)** 45 minutes

**By the end you can** build operating costs and the payables roll-forward.
:::

**Purpose.** Build operating costs (variable handling, fixed handling, fixed O&M with a live sensitivity) and the payables roll-forward that converts cost to cash paid.

**Concept.** Variable handling = cost per arrival x arrivals / 1,000 x escalation. Fixed handling and O&M are annual amounts divided by 4 and escalated. O&M is multiplied by (1 + sensitivity): row 28 pulls InpC row 46 (0% Base and Upside, +10% Downside). Payables mirror receivables: cash paid = opening payables + (days - payable days)/days x cost.

### Inputs used

| Input | Where | Base | Downside | Upside | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Handling cost- fixed per annum | InpC row 42 | 4,500 | 4,500 | 4,500 | $ 000s |
| Handling cost - variable | InpC row 44 | 550 | 550 | 550 | USD/arrival |
| O&M cost- fixed per annum | InpC row 48 | 3,300 | 3,300 | 3,300 | $ 000s |
| Account payables days | InpC row 50 | 35 | 35 | 35 | days |
| CPI index at handling signature date | InpC row 25 | 120 | 120 | 120 | index |
| CPI index at O&M signature date | InpC row 27 | 132 | 132 | 132 | index |


### Build order

1. Pull the drivers: unit, arrivals, escalation, forecast flag.
2. Row 16: =IF(J15=1,$F11/$F12\*J13\*J14,0). Row 23: =IF(J22=1,$F19/$F20\*J21,0). Row 31: =IF(J30=1,$F26/$F27\*J29\*(1+$F28),0).
3. Row 38 operating cost POS = SUM(J35:J37); row 39 = -1 x row 38 (IS).
4. Row 46 cash paid for invoices: =(J44-$F43)/J44\*J45; row 50 = opening payables + row 46; row 51 = -1 x row 50 (CF).
5. Row 62 payables: =IF(J57=1,$F56,J59+J60-J61).

```text
ROLE
You are a senior Python engineer who builds auditable Excel models with openpyxl.

TASK
Write a function build_sheet(wb, spec) that creates or completes this block in an openpyxl workbook: OpCost: handling, O&M, payables (sheet or sheets: OpCost) using exactly the specification below. Return a list of (cell, expected_value, tolerance) checks so that I can test the workbook after recalculation in Excel.
Purpose: Build operating costs (variable handling, fixed handling, fixed O&M with a live sensitivity) and the payables roll-forward that converts cost to cash paid.

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

openpyxl 3.1 writes formulas as text and never calculates them; recalculation happens in Excel. Use _xlfn. for MINIFS, XLOOKUP and similar. Avoid array formulas; where the course workbook shows braces use a plain INDEX formula. Keep the workbook under 1 MB: never touch cells beyond column CO.

Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Cost inflation | Add a cost multiplier (all operating costs +10%). | Blended sponsor IRR falls from 43.0% to 28.7% (see the sensitivity table). |
| Semi-fixed costs | Add a step-fixed cost row by trains. | Insert a row above row 38 and extend the SUM range inside it (Excel updates references on insert, never cut and paste). |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| O&M sensitivity has no effect | Row 28 not pulled or not inside the formula | Use $F28 inside (1+$F28) |
| Costs paid exceed costs incurred forever | Payables roll-forward missing the opening balance | BEG row must link to the previous closing |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why is O&M multiplied by (1 + sensitivity)?
   *Answer:* To let one input shock the cost line in a scenario without editing the contract amount.
2. Why do payables mirror receivables?
   *Answer:* Suppliers are paid after the payable days, so cash paid lags cost incurred in the same way receipts lag revenue.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: O&M sensitivity has no effect. *Likely cause and fix:* Row 28 not pulled or not inside the formula. Use $F28 inside (1+$F28).
2. You see: Costs paid exceed costs incurred forever. *Likely cause and fix:* Payables roll-forward missing the opening balance. BEG row must link to the previous closing.
:::


## B06 Tax: depreciation, taxable income, cash tax, deferred tax {#sec-b06}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 4 · **Sheet(s)** Tax · **Depends on** B02, B05, B07 (NCA) and B08 (Debt interest) · **Produces** Row 32 tax paid (CF); row 38 tax expense (IS); row 49 deferred tax (BS) · **Suggested time (Path A)** 45 minutes

**By the end you can** explain and build cash tax, tax expense and deferred tax, and why they differ.
:::

**Purpose.** Compute tax depreciation on a written-down-value basis, taxable income net of interest, cash tax paid, the P&L tax expense and the deferred-tax balance.

**Concept.** Cash tax = 30% x (EBITDA - tax depreciation - interest). Tax expense in the income statement = 30% x profit before tax (accounting depreciation and interest). The difference accumulates as deferred tax = cumulative expense - cumulative paid, which must unwind to zero by the last quarter. Tax depreciation is 5% of the written-down value per QUARTER (about 18.5% a year). Taxable losses are refunded in cash in the quarter they arise (the workbook has no loss carry-forward): 4 quarters in Base and 11 in Downside; this flatters Downside CFADS and cover (app option 'carry losses forward': Downside minimum DSCR 2.34x becomes 2.25x and NPV falls from -7,231 to -7,523). Tax law is jurisdiction-specific; see the caveats chapter. The original file left the interest placeholder (Tax row 26) empty, so deferred tax stayed stranded in retained earnings; the corrected model links row 26 to the senior-debt interest (and, in the PF model, to the shareholder-loan interest).

### Inputs used

| Input | Where | Base | Downside | Upside | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tax depreciation rate | InpC row 84 | 5.0% | 5.0% | 5.0% | % TWDV |
| Corporation tax rate | InpC row 86 | 30.0% | 30.0% | 30.0% | % |
| Non current asset - initial balance | InpC row 64 | 101,068 | 101,068 | 101,068 | $ 000s |


### Build order

1. Tax WDV roll-forward (rows 15 to 21): opening + capex - tax depreciation; tax depreciation = 5% x opening balance, written off entirely in the last forecast period (row 11).
2. Taxable income (rows 24 to 27): EBITDA (FinStat row 11) - tax depreciation - interest (row 26 pulls Debt interest).
3. Tax paid POS = 30% x taxable income (row 31), row 32 = -1 x row 31 (CF). Tax expense POS = 30% x PBT (FinStat row 15); row 38 = -1 x POS (IS).
4. Deferred tax roll-forward: opening + tax expense - tax paid (row 49).

```text
ROLE
You are a quantitative developer building an independent replica of a spreadsheet block to prove it is right.

TASK

Purpose: Compute tax depreciation on a written-down-value basis, taxable income net of interest, cash tax paid, the P&L tax expense and the deferred-tax balance.
How the block works: Cash tax = 30% x (EBITDA - tax depreciation - interest). Tax expense in the income statement = 30% x profit before tax (accounting depreciation and interest). The difference accumulates as deferred tax = cumulative expense - cumulative paid, which must unwind to zero by the last quarter. Tax depreciation is 5% of the written-down value per QUARTER (about 18.5% a year). Taxable losses are refunded in cash in the quarter they arise (the workbook has no loss carry-forward): 4 quarters in Base and 11 in Downside; this flatters Downside CFADS and cover (app option 'carry losses forward': Downside minimum DSCR 2.34x becomes 2.25x and NPV falls from -7,231 to -7,523). Tax law is jurisdiction-specific; see the caveats chapter. The original file left the interest placeholder (Tax row 26) empty, so deferred tax stayed stranded in retained earnings; the corrected model links row 26 to the senior-debt interest (and, in the PF model, to the shareholder-loan interest).

### Checkpoints

- Tax!H11 = 108,000; H27 = 662,904; H31 = 198,871; H37 = 198,871 (start model, Base)
- Tax!H31 = Tax!H37: nothing stranded
- Deferred tax balance (row 49) is zero at CO

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Interest deductibility OFF | Set the interest row to 0 (the original file). | Cash tax rises, deferred tax ends at a stranded balance (see Option atlas) and the shareholder IRR falls. |
| Loss carry-forward | Add a loss balance row and pay tax only on taxable income after losses (app option). | Removes cash refunds. Downside: minimum DSCR 2.34x to 2.25x, NPV -7,231 to -7,523; Base: IRR 43.03% to 42.91%. |
| Straight-line tax depreciation | Replace the 5% WDV by asset life / periods. | Tax shield is more front-loaded under WDV; NPV falls slightly under straight line. |
| Thin-capitalisation or interest-cap rule | Cap deductible interest at 30% of EBITDA. | Replace the interest row by MIN(interest, 30% x EBITDA); check the sizing CFADS in B16 which uses tax before interest. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Deferred tax does not return to zero | Row 26 interest not linked | Link Tax row 26 to Debt interest (and SHL interest in the PF model) |
| Negative tax paid | Taxable income negative in early years | The workbook refunds losses in cash (a teaching simplification); add a loss roll-forward to carry them forward |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why do tax paid and tax expense differ?
   *Answer:* Cash tax uses tax depreciation and deducts interest; the income statement uses accounting depreciation; the difference accumulates as deferred tax.
2. What does a stranded deferred-tax balance tell you?
   *Answer:* That one tax line omits an item (here interest), so tax paid and tax expense never converge.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: Deferred tax does not return to zero. *Likely cause and fix:* Row 26 interest not linked. Link Tax row 26 to Debt interest (and SHL interest in the PF model).
2. You see: Negative tax paid. *Likely cause and fix:* Taxable income negative in early years. The workbook refunds losses in cash (a teaching simplification); add a loss roll-forward to carry them forward.
:::


## B07 NCA: capex, depreciation and the asset balance {#sec-b07}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 5 (Tue 20 Oct) · **Sheet(s)** NCA · **Depends on** B01, B02 · **Produces** Row 54 accounting depreciation (IS); row 64 non-current asset balance (BS); row 19 capital expenditure (CF) · **Suggested time (Path A)** 50 minutes

**By the end you can** depreciate opening assets and new capex and roll the asset balance.
:::

**Purpose.** Hold the capex table, depreciate the opening assets straight line over 15 years, depreciate new capex as a pool over its 5-year life, and roll the asset balance.

**Concept.** Opening assets of US$100,000k (US$101,068k after construction in the PF model) are depreciated straight line over 15 years = 60 quarters. New capex enters a pool that is depreciated at pool / 20 each quarter and retires after 20 quarters (SUMIFS on the column counter). This pool method is a deliberate simplification of asset-by-asset depreciation.

### Inputs used

| Input | Where | Base | Downside | Upside | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non current asset - initial balance | InpC row 64 | 101,068 | 101,068 | 101,068 | $ 000s |
| Useful life of NCA at acquisition | InpC row 65 | 15 | 15 | 15 | years |
| Useful life -capex | InpC row 67 | 5 | 5 | 5 | yrs |


### Build order

1. Capex POS (row 18): =IFNA(VLOOKUP(J17,$E$10:$F$16,2,FALSE),0); row 19 = -1 x row 18 (CF).
2. Initial-balance depreciation (row 29): =IF(J28=1,$F25/($F26\*$F27),0).
3. Retirement (row 39): =SUMIFS($J38:J38,$J37:J37,J37-$F36) (an expanding range: sum the capex made exactly 20 periods ago). Pool BEG/END (rows 41 to 44); capex depreciation (row 48) = pool BEG / periodic life.
4. Summary: row 53 = SUM of rows 51:52; row 54 = -1 x row 53 (IS).
5. Asset balance (row 64): =IF(J59=1,$F58,J61+J62-J63).

### Specification (40 rows)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show the row-by-row specification"}
Format: sheet row | label | formulas | totals (H) and first-forecast-quarter values (L) from the verified workbook.

TASK
