#### A Tutor

::: {.prompt}
```text
ROLE
You are a patient Excel modelling tutor on the Mastering Infrastructure and Project Finance Boot Camp (Lagos Business School). You coach; you do not do the work for me.

TASK
I am building this block of the TrainStat project-finance model in Excel on Windows or Mac: Integration: FinStat, Tax, Equity and Val for the PF structure (sheet or sheets: FinStat, Val).
Purpose: Insert the rows that the new sheets need in FinStat (SHL interest, DSRA, SHL cash flows, SHL liability), widen the SUM ranges, and make Val use the blended cash flows.
Prerequisites already built and passing their checks: B14 to B20
What this block must deliver: Final FinStat rows (checks F80, F83, F86), Val NPV F41 and XIRR F51

MODEL CHARTER (applies to every row)
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

INPUT VALUES FOR THIS BUILD
```

```text
ROLE
You are an Excel formula generator for a quarterly project-finance model. You output exact, paste-ready formulas and nothing speculative.

TASK
Produce every formula needed for this block of the TrainStat model: Integration: FinStat, Tax, Equity and Val for the PF structure (sheet or sheets: FinStat, Val). Excel version: Microsoft 365 or 2019 on Windows or Mac. Allowed functions: only those that appear in the specification of the model, namely ABS, AND, AVERAGEIFS, DATE, DAY, EOMONTH, IF, IFNA, INDEX, MATCH, MAX, MIN, MINIFS, MONTH, SUM, SUMIFS, SUMPRODUCT, TEXT, VLOOKUP, XIRR, YEAR, FORMULATEXT. Forbidden: OFFSET, INDIRECT, volatile functions, macros, circular references, iterative calculation.
Purpose: Insert the rows that the new sheets need in FinStat (SHL interest, DSRA, SHL cash flows, SHL liability), widen the SUM ranges, and make Val use the blended cash flows.

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).
```

```text
ROLE
You are a senior Python engineer who builds auditable Excel models with openpyxl.

TASK
Write a function build_sheet(wb, spec) that creates or completes this block in an openpyxl workbook: Integration: FinStat, Tax, Equity and Val for the PF structure (sheet or sheets: FinStat, Val) using exactly the specification below. Return a list of (cell, expected_value, tolerance) checks so that I can test the workbook after recalculation in Excel.
Purpose: Insert the rows that the new sheets need in FinStat (SHL interest, DSRA, SHL cash flows, SHL liability), widen the SUM ranges, and make Val use the blended cash flows.

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

TOOL FACTS
openpyxl 3.1 writes formulas as text and never calculates them; recalculation happens in Excel. Use _xlfn. for MINIFS, XLOOKUP and similar. Avoid array formulas; where the course workbook shows braces use a plain INDEX formula. Keep the workbook under 1 MB: never touch cells beyond column CO.
```

```text
ROLE
You are an independent model auditor (FAST standard, financial-modelling review). You do not trust labels; you test.

TASK
Audit this block of my TrainStat workbook: Integration: FinStat, Tax, Equity and Val for the PF structure (sheet or sheets: FinStat, Val) against the specification and checkpoints below. I will paste a dump of the sheet: for each row the label, column F, the formulas in J, K and L (as typed), the total in H and the value in L. (How to make the dump: in a spare column type =FORMULATEXT(J11) and fill down the rows, or press Ctrl+` and copy the sheet, plus a values copy of columns E, F, H and L. The charter below lists the documented exceptions; do not report them as faults.)

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).
```

### Checkpoints

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Rebuild FinStat on a new sheet | Create FinStat2 with the new layout. | No insert risk, but every downstream link must be re-pointed manually. |
| Use structured references | Convert the timeline block to an Excel Table. | Not recommended: tables fight with row-wise time series. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Balance sheet check = 1 after inserting rows | A SUM range did not grow | Edit the SUM ranges of the subtotals |
| #REF! after inserting | A row was cut and pasted | Undo; copy, paste and then delete the original |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why insert rows rather than cut and paste?
   *Answer:* Inserting lets Excel update every reference; cutting and pasting can break them.
2. Which ranges do not grow automatically?
   *Answer:* SUM ranges when the new row sits at the edge of the range.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: Balance sheet check = 1 after inserting rows. *Likely cause and fix:* A SUM range did not grow. Edit the SUM ranges of the subtotals.
2. You see: #REF! after inserting. *Likely cause and fix:* A row was cut and pasted. Undo; copy, paste and then delete the original.
:::


## B22 Optimisation: Goal Seek, data tables and the structure grid {#sec-b22}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 7 · **Sheet(s)** workbook structure · **Depends on** B16 to B21 · **Produces** A defensible structure (target DSCR, tenor, gearing, DSRA, SHL) and a one-paragraph recommendation · **Suggested time (Path A)** 45 minutes

**By the end you can** choose and defend a capital structure from a grid.
:::

**Purpose.** Choose the capital structure that maximises the sponsor return within the lender's tests, and defend it.

**Concept.** Raising the target DSCR or shortening the tenor reduces debt capacity; the gearing cap limits it from above. The sponsor IRR rises with leverage until the gearing cap binds, then is flat in the DSCR target (46.86% for 1.75x and 2.00x at 40 quarters: the cap, not the DSCR, limits debt). The lender's view: minimum actual DSCR stays above target because actual CFADS includes the interest tax shield. Sponsors propose the structure that maximises their return within the term sheet; the credit committee approves it only if it is bankable under the lender's case and the downside (see the scenarios on the FIXED financing in the options atlas).

### Inputs used

| Input | Where | Base | Downside | Upside | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target DSCR for sculpting | InpC row 140 | 2.25x | 2.25x | 2.25x | x |
| Senior debt tenor | InpC row 139 | 40 | 40 | 40 | quarters |
| Maximum gearing (debt / total uses) | InpC row 141 | 75% | 75% | 75% | % |
| DSRA cover (periods of debt service) | InpC row 143 | 2 | 2 | 2 | periods |
| Shareholder loan share of sponsor funding | InpC row 147 | 60% | 60% | 60% | % |


### Build order

1. Run Goal Seek (B16) for each (DSCR, tenor) of interest; record gearing, debt, minimum DSCR, blended IRR.
2. Optional: a two-way data table on InpC row 140 (target DSCR) and row 139 (tenor) of Val!F51; Goal Seek must be re-run for each cell, so use the table to shortlist.
3. Write the recommendation: 'We propose X because it meets the lender's DSCR, LLCR and gearing tests and returns Y% to sponsors.'

### Prompts

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### A Tutor

::: {.prompt}
```text
ROLE
You are a patient Excel modelling tutor on the Mastering Infrastructure and Project Finance Boot Camp (Lagos Business School). You coach; you do not do the work for me.

TASK
I am building this block of the TrainStat project-finance model in Excel on Windows or Mac: Optimisation: Goal Seek, data tables and the structure grid (sheet or sheets: the workbook structure).
Purpose: Choose the capital structure that maximises the sponsor return within the lender's tests, and defend it.
Prerequisites already built and passing their checks: B16 to B21
What this block must deliver: A defensible structure (target DSCR, tenor, gearing, DSRA, SHL) and a one-paragraph recommendation

MODEL CHARTER (applies to every row)
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

INPUT VALUES FOR THIS BUILD
- Target DSCR for sculpting (InpC row 140): 2.25x
- Senior debt tenor (InpC row 139): 40 quarters
- Maximum gearing (debt / total uses) (InpC row 141): 75%
- DSRA cover (periods of debt service) (InpC row 143): 2 periods
- Shareholder loan share of sponsor funding (InpC row 147): 60%

SPECIFICATION (row | label | formula in the constant column F and in the first timeline column J | exceptions)
(structural block: no row specification; follow the build order below)
1. Run Goal Seek (B16) for each (DSCR, tenor) of interest; record gearing, debt, minimum DSCR, blended IRR.
2. Optional: a two-way data table on InpC row 140 (target DSCR) and row 139 (tenor) of Val!F51; Goal Seek must be re-run for each cell, so use the table to shortlist.
3. Write the recommendation: 'We propose X because it meets the lender's DSCR, LLCR and gearing tests and returns Y% to sponsors.'

HOW YOU MUST TEACH

For every action show the keystrokes for Windows and Mac (for example Go To: Ctrl+G on both; fill a selected range with the typed formula: Ctrl+Enter on Windows, Ctrl+Return on Mac; fill right from the first cell: Ctrl+R on Windows, Cmd+R on Mac; cycle the $ signs: F4 on Windows, Cmd+T or Fn+F4 on Mac; show formulas: Ctrl+` on both).

5. At the end ask me five check questions on this block, one at a time, and mark my answers.

START
Confirm the prerequisites, then ask me which row I want to begin with.
```

### Checkpoints

- Grid values (Base): 2.25x / 40 quarters -> debt 72,154, gearing 71.4%, min DSCR 2.30x, IRR 43.0%
- 2.00x / 40 quarters -> debt 76,052 (cap binds), gearing 75.0%, min DSCR 2.18x, IRR 46.86%; 2.25x / 48 quarters -> debt 76,052, min DSCR 2.57x, IRR 46.55%

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Maximise IRR s.t. min DSCR >= 2.0x | Search the grid. | 1.75x or 2.00x at 40 quarters (cap binds, 75% gearing) give the highest IRR, 46.86%, with minimum DSCR 2.18x; 2.25x at 40 quarters gives 43.03% at 2.30x. |
| What a credit committee weighs | Compare the best structure with its own fixed-financing downside. | The 2.00x / 40-quarter structure (75% gearing; with tax refunds the IRR is 46.86% from COD; with losses carried forward, the basis of the following figures, it is 46.68% from COD and 37.1% dated at the contributions) has a Downside minimum DSCR of 1.35x on a quarterly basis (1.59x rolling 12 months). On the fixed financing the fare can fall 11.9% (quarterly basis) or 16.0% (rolling 12-month basis) before cover reaches the 1.20x lock-up, and 13.7% or 18.6% before 1.00x (carry-forward). The 2.25x structure gives 43.03% from COD (42.91% with carry-forward), a quarterly Downside minimum of 1.43x and breakevens of 12.5% (quarterly) and 16.8% (rolling) to the 1.20x lock-up. The extra 3.8 points of IRR are bought with thinner cover. |
| Maximise NPV instead | Use the NPV at the hurdle. | IRR and NPV can rank structures differently; check both. On this grid the same structures lead (NPV about 30,477). |
| Solver (non-linear) | Use Excel Solver with constraints. | Handles several variables, but needs the Goal Seek step inside each evaluation; use a macro or the replica. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Data table gives IRR that cannot be reproduced | Gearing not re-solved per cell | Use the table to shortlist; confirm with Goal Seek |
| Recommendation ignores the downside | Only Base examined | Test the Downside and the breakeven fare on the FIXED financing (options atlas, 'Debt sized once'), not on a re-sized case |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why is IRR flat in the DSCR target once the cap binds?
   *Answer:* The gearing cap, not the DSCR, limits debt, so loosening the DSCR adds no debt.
2. Why is a higher IRR not enough to approve a structure?
   *Answer:* The credit committee tests the structure on the lender's case and the downside, on a fixed financing.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: Data table gives IRR that cannot be reproduced. *Likely cause and fix:* Gearing not re-solved per cell. Use the table to shortlist; confirm with Goal Seek.
2. You see: Recommendation ignores the downside. *Likely cause and fix:* Only Base examined. Test the Downside and the breakeven fare on the FIXED financing (options atlas, 'Debt sized once'), not on a re-sized case.
:::


## B23 Cover, Dashboard, audit and handover {#sec-b23}

::: {.block-meta}
**Day** 7 · **Sheet(s)** workbook structure · **Depends on** Everything · **Produces** Cover sheet (status, scenario note, debt-sizing status, sheet guide, change log), Dashboard (KPI tiles, annual summary 2022 to 2041, four charts), model guide · **Suggested time (Path A)** 45 minutes

**By the end you can** hand over a model that a stranger can run from its guide.
:::

**Purpose.** Make the model usable by someone else: a cover with the status line, scenario definitions and change log; a dashboard of the headline results; an audit pass; a handover pack.

**Concept.** A model that cannot be run by a stranger from its guide in 30 minutes is not finished. In the delivered workbook the Cover status reads ALL CHECKS PASSED only when the three FinStat checks, the Time modelling-period check (Time!F120), the Constr opening-balance check (F55) and the Constr sources-less-uses row (48) are all zero; in the PF model a second line reads 'Debt drawn equals debt sized' only when Sculpt!F32 is within 1 (otherwise RE-RUN GOAL SEEK). Treat these two lines as the minimum; the audit pass below covers everything else (debt repaid, shareholder loan repaid, deferred tax unwound).

### Build order

1. Cover: title, course and contact line, the status formula =IF(FinStat!F80+FinStat!F83+FinStat!F86+Time!F120=0,"ALL CHECKS PASSED","CHECK ERRORS: see FinStat") (PF row numbers), the active scenario =InpC!F3, a scenario-definition note, the debt-sizing status (Sculpt!F32), a sheet guide, how-to-run steps and the change log of every correction.
2. Dashboard: guard every ratio against a zero or float-noise denominator with the named tolerance, for example =IF(ABS(debt service)>CHK_TOL,CFADS/debt service,0) (without it the DSCR row showed values of -1e16 after maturity); KPI tiles (shareholder NPV =Val!F41, XIRR =Val!F51, minimum DSCR =Ratios!F13, total CFADS =Track!H10, senior debt at close =Debt!F11, project cost at COD =Constr!F52, gearing at COD =Constr!F53/Constr!F52, LLCR at COD =Ratios!F22); an annual summary built with SUMIFS on the financial-year row of FinStat (revenue, cost, EBITDA, CFADS, debt service, dividends, DSCR); four charts (revenue and EBITDA, CFADS and debt service, DSCR by year, dividends by year).
3. Audit: Ctrl+` shows formulas; Home > Find & Select > Go To Special > Constants finds typed numbers inside calculation sheets; Formulas > Error Checking; select a row and press Ctrl+\ to find cells that differ from the first one (consistency across J to CO).
4. Run the integrity list: debt balance zero at CO, shareholder loan balance zero, deferred tax zero, DSRA zero, Constr!H48 = 0, Sculpt!F32 about 0, no error values in any sheet (Find All on # with Look in = Values).
5. Handover: save v-final, export Cover and Dashboard to PDF, store the model guide next to the file.

```text
ROLE
You are an Excel formula generator for a quarterly project-finance model. You output exact, paste-ready formulas and nothing speculative.

TASK
Produce every formula needed for this block of the TrainStat model: Cover, Dashboard, audit and handover (sheet or sheets: the workbook structure). Excel version: Microsoft 365 or 2019 on Windows or Mac. Allowed functions: only those that appear in the specification of the model, namely ABS, AND, AVERAGEIFS, DATE, DAY, EOMONTH, IF, IFNA, INDEX, MATCH, MAX, MIN, MINIFS, MONTH, SUM, SUMIFS, SUMPRODUCT, TEXT, VLOOKUP, XIRR, YEAR, FORMULATEXT. Forbidden: OFFSET, INDIRECT, volatile functions, macros, circular references, iterative calculation.
Purpose: Make the model usable by someone else: a cover with the status line, scenario definitions and change log; a dashboard of the headline results; an audit pass; a handover pack.

MODEL CHARTER
You are building a quarterly project-finance model in Microsoft Excel for the TrainStat teaching case (US$ thousands).
Conventions that apply to every sheet (do not deviate):
1. Layout: column E = row label, F = constant, G = unit, H = row total (sum of the timeline; blank or 0 where a total is meaningless), J to CO = 84 quarterly columns (J = 30 Sep 2021, K = COD 31 Dec 2021, L onward = forecast to 31 Dec 2041). Rows 2 to 5 of every calculation sheet pull the date, phase label, financial year and column counter from Time. The one exception is Constr, which has its own 8-column construction timeline (J to Q, 31 Mar 2020 to COD 31 Dec 2021).
2. Pull-then-calculate: as a rule a calculation does not reach into another sheet inside a formula. First pull each driver into a visible row on the same sheet (blue font), then calculate in the next row (red font for result rows). Typed inputs live only on InpC (constants, per scenario) and InpS (time series) and are filled yellow. A few project-finance rows combine pulls inside one formula (for example Sculpt row 20, Tax row 26, SHL row 16); these appear in the specification and are the only exceptions.
3. One formula per row: the formula in J must be the same R1C1 formula across J to CO. The only allowed exceptions are the first-column cases listed in the spec.
4. No numbers typed inside formulas except 0, 1, -1 and the documented XIRR device (-0.001 in the first column of Val). Units (1,000), periods per year (4), day count (360), days per year (365) and the tolerance come from InpC. Documented small exceptions: 12 months per year in Time!F64, the column numbers inside VLOOKUP and INDEX, and the audit-stamp cells on Track (H2, H72:H74) that use TODAY, NOW and CELL and feed nothing.
5. Roll-forward identity for every balance: closing = opening + additions - reductions; the opening balance in column J is the previous column's closing balance, except on the acquisition date where it equals the initial balance input.
6. Rows named "... POS" are positive numbers; the next row flips the sign for the statements (IS, CF) or leaves it (BS).
7. Checks return 0 when the model is correct (a flag of 1 per failing column, summed in column F; Time!F120 is a similar total check and Constr row 48 is a sources-less-uses difference that must be zero in every quarter). Tolerance is the named range CHK_TOL (0.001).
8. Scenarios are chosen on InpC!F3; F4 = MATCH(F3, I3:M3, 0); every constant in column F is =INDEX(I:M row, $F$4).

INPUT VALUES FOR THIS BUILD
- (no numeric inputs: this block is structural)

SPECIFICATION
(structural block: no row specification; follow the build order below)
1. Cover: title, course and contact line, the status formula =IF(FinStat!F80+FinStat!F83+FinStat!F86+Time!F120=0,"ALL CHECKS PASSED","CHECK ERRORS: see FinStat") (PF row numbers), the active scenario =InpC!F3, a scenario-definition note, the debt-sizing status (Sculpt!F32), a sheet guide, how-to-run steps and the change log of every correction.
2. Dashboard: guard every ratio against a zero or float-noise denominator with the named tolerance, for example =IF(ABS(debt service)>CHK_TOL,CFADS/debt service,0) (without it the DSCR row showed values of -1e16 after maturity); KPI tiles (shareholder NPV =Val!F41, XIRR =Val!F51, minimum DSCR =Ratios!F13, total CFADS =Track!H10, senior debt at close =Debt!F11, project cost at COD =Constr!F52, gearing at COD =Constr!F53/Constr!F52, LLCR at COD =Ratios!F22); an annual summary built with SUMIFS on the financial-year row of FinStat (revenue, cost, EBITDA, CFADS, debt service, dividends, DSCR); four charts (revenue and EBITDA, CFADS and debt service, DSCR by year, dividends by year).
3. Audit: Ctrl+` shows formulas; Home > Find & Select > Go To Special > Constants finds typed numbers inside calculation sheets; Formulas > Error Checking; select a row and press Ctrl+\ to find cells that differ from the first one (consistency across J to CO).
4. Run the integrity list: debt balance zero at CO, shareholder loan balance zero, deferred tax zero, DSRA zero, Constr!H48 = 0, Sculpt!F32 about 0, no error values in any sheet (Find All on # with Look in = Values).
5. Handover: save v-final, export Cover and Dashboard to PDF, store the model guide next to the file.

CHECKPOINTS
- Cover status reads ALL CHECKS PASSED in all three scenarios (after Goal Seek has been re-run for the active scenario)
- Zero error cells (#N/A, #REF!, #NAME?, #DIV/0!) across all sheets
- File size under 1 MB


OUTPUT FORMAT
1. A table with columns: Cell | Formula to type | How to fill (range and keystrokes for Windows and Mac) | Number format | Expected value in column L | Expected total in column H.
2. One line per row of the specification, in order; pulls first, calculations second, subtotals last.
3. After the table, list the three most likely mistakes in this block and how a check would reveal each.
4. Do not invent rows or change row numbers. If the specification is ambiguous, ask me before answering.
```

### Checkpoints

- Cover status reads ALL CHECKS PASSED in all three scenarios (after Goal Seek has been re-run for the active scenario)
- Zero error cells (#N/A, #REF!, #NAME?, #DIV/0!) across all sheets
- File size under 1 MB

### Options and alternative paths

| Option | How to change the build | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Lock sheets | Protect formulas, leave inputs unlocked. | Prevents accidental overwrite; keep the password with the guide. |
| Publish a read-only HTML dashboard | Export the results to JSON and render them with this app. | Lets lenders explore without Excel. |
| Stronger status line | Add the integrity list above to the status formula. | The delivered workbook keeps the minimal status; adding the other tests makes the Cover the single place to look. |

### Failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard stale after changing scenario | Charts point at stored runs (Track M:O) | Point charts at live results (FinStat rows via SUMIFS) |
| Cover says passed but a sheet is broken | A check not included in the status formula | Run the integrity list; extend the formula |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-check: concept questions and what to do when it breaks"}
**Concept questions**

1. Why guard ratios with the tolerance?
   *Answer:* Float noise after maturity makes a zero denominator look non-zero and produces nonsense ratios.
2. What is the minimum content of the Cover status?
   *Answer:* Every check that should be zero: statements, timeline, opening balances and sources-less-uses.

**When it breaks**

1. You see: Dashboard stale after changing scenario. *Likely cause and fix:* Charts point at stored runs (Track M:O). Point charts at live results (FinStat rows via SUMIFS).
2. You see: Cover says passed but a sheet is broken. *Likely cause and fix:* A check not included in the status formula. Run the integrity list; extend the formula.
:::


# Options atlas: what changes the answer {#sec-options}

All figures are the Base scenario of the project-finance model, re-solved for each option (gearing found so that debt drawn equals debt sized), computed by the engine in `mipf_model_builder.html`. Where an option is not in the delivered workbook it is marked *app only*.

## Drawdown and interest during construction

IRR and NPV in this table are measured from COD, as in the workbook (convention R1). Equity first looks better from COD; **dated at the contributions the ranking reverses** (see "Sponsor IRR: measured from COD versus dated" below).

| Option | Project cost | Senior debt | Gearing | Min DSCR | Blended IRR (from COD, R1) | NPV @25.25% (from COD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pro-rata, interest on opening balance (course) | 101,068 | 72,154 | 71.39% | 2.30x | 43.03% | 28,244 |
| Equity first, opening-balance interest | 100,115 | 72,065 | 71.98% | 2.30x | 44.19% | 29,155 |
| Equity first, average-balance interest (*app only*) | 100,695 | 72,119 | 71.62% | 2.30x | 43.48% | 28,601 |
| Pro-rata, average-balance interest (algebraic, *app only* in the solved case) | 101,668 | 72,210 | 71.03% | 2.30x | 42.34% | 27,667 |


Teaching case on Day 6 (facility 60,000, gearing 60%, hard cost 94,850):

| Method | IDC | Commitment fee | Total uses | Debt at COD | Equity at COD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pro-rata, opening balance | 3,458.2 | 514.7 | 100,022.9 | 60,013.8 | 40,009.2 |
| Pro-rata, average balance | 3,972.9 | 512.7 | 100,535.6 | 60,321.3 | 40,214.2 |
| Equity first | 2,212.6 | 658.4 | 98,921.1 | 58,921.1 | 40,000.0 |
| Equity first, average balance | 2,719.9 | 656.3 | 99,426.2 | 59,426.2 | 40,000.0 |


## Repayment style (same debt size, different shape)

The debt is sized once on the sculpting capacity (target 2.25x over 40 quarters); the other shapes then repay that debt. They show why sculpting exists: with the same debt, a straight-line profile collapses cover in the weakest quarters. Profile 2 shows a higher IRR at a minimum DSCR of about 1.2x: that is not bankable at this debt size (below typical sizing levels and near lock-up); lenders limit back-ended profiles through average-life and tail requirements. These rows are *app only*: in the workbook the shareholder loan is repaid after the Sculpt tenor, so with profiles 2 and 3 it can be repaid while senior debt is still outstanding.

| Repayment | Debt | Min DSCR | Average DSCR | Last repayment quarter | Blended IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sculpted (profile 4) | 72,154 | 2.30x | 2.40x | 40 | 43.03% |
| Profile 1 (7.5 years straight line) | 72,154 | 1.03x | 2.21x | 33 | 41.47% |
| Profile 2 (10 years) | 72,154 | 1.23x | 2.81x | 43 | 43.88% |
| Profile 3 (15 years) | 72,154 | 1.53x | 4.14x | 63 | 42.97% |

## Debt sized once: scenarios tested on the fixed Base financing

A credit committee does not re-size the debt in each scenario. Debt size and the sculpted repayment schedule are frozen at the Base case; cash flows, tax and cover are recomputed. *Refund* is the workbook's treatment of tax losses; *carry-forward* is the app option. Covenants are usually tested at each calculation date on a historic 12-month basis (and often also a projected one; LLCR tests use the projections), so both the single-quarter minimum (stricter; the weakest quarter is the 31 Dec 2023 capex quarter) and the rolling 12-month minimum are shown. IRRs marked * ignore lock-up and default consequences, which the model does not contain: in those cases distributions would be blocked.

| Case on the Base financing | Min DSCR, quarter (refund) | Min DSCR, quarter (carry-forward) | Min DSCR, rolling 12 months (carry-forward) | Average DSCR | LLCR at COD | Blended IRR from COD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Downside | 1.68x | 1.43x | 1.67x | 1.83x | 1.84x | 27.49% |
| Upside | 2.76x | 2.76x | 2.83x | 2.94x | 2.93x | 60.13% |
| Base fare -15% | 1.30x | 0.90x | 1.34x | 1.59x | 1.60x | 21.92% |
| Base fare -20% | 0.88x | 0.29x | 0.94x | 1.32x | 1.34x | 16.80% *; negative cash, indicative only |
| Base fare -25% | 0.46x | -0.32x | 0.55x | 1.06x | 1.09x | 12.24% *; negative cash, indicative only |
| Base O&M +20% | 2.24x | 2.23x | 2.25x | 2.34x | 2.34x | 41.21% |

Breakeven fare (Base financing, carry-forward): the **single-quarter** minimum DSCR reaches 1.20x at a fare **12.5% below** Base and 1.00x at **14.1% below**; on the **rolling 12-month** basis the figures are **16.8%** and **19.3%** (with tax refunds: quarter 16.2% and 18.6%; rolling 20.9% and 24.9%). A credit agreement tests the rolling basis, so a fare 12.5% below Base would not by itself be a lock-up event; lumpy capex is normally smoothed through a major-maintenance reserve account. The re-solved Downside (minimum DSCR 2.34x) looks safer than the Downside on the Base financing (1.43x quarterly, 1.67x rolling) because the lenders have already lent less.


## Sponsor IRR: measured from COD versus dated at the contribution dates

The workbook (Val) dates all sponsor funding at COD, although equity is paid in during construction. The app reports both.

| Case (Base) | Blended IRR from COD (workbook) | Blended IRR dated at contributions | Project cost | Sponsor funding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pro-rata, opening-balance interest (course) | 43.03% | 34.71% | 101,068 | 28,914 |
| Equity first | 44.19% | 32.03% | 100,115 | 28,050 |
| Equity first, average-balance interest | 43.48% | 31.68% | 100,695 | 28,575 |
| Pro-rata, average-balance interest | 42.34% | 34.27% | 101,668 | 29,457 |

From COD, equity first looks better; dated at the contributions it is worse for the sponsor, which is why sponsors negotiate pro-rata drawdown or letters of credit for undrawn equity.

# Diagnostic prompts {#sec-diag}

Use these when a check fails. Replace the <<...>> placeholders with your own values.


**Balance sheet check = 1**

::: {.prompt}
```text
I have a balance sheet check (FinStat row 80/86) that equals 1 in <<column>> and 0 elsewhere. Here are the movements of every balance sheet row in the column before and in that column: <<paste here>>. Find the row whose change is not explained by the cash flow or income statement. Return the suspected row, the reason (sign, range, missing link, timing) and the exact formula fix.
```
:::


**Sources not equal to uses**

::: {.prompt}
```text
Constr row 48 is not zero in quarter <<quarter>>. Here are rows 35 to 47 for that quarter: <<paste here>>. Identify the wrong row (equity formula range, drawdown switch, fee timing) and give the corrected formula.
```
:::


**Circular reference warning**

::: {.prompt}
```text
Excel reports a circular reference. Here is the list of cells in the cycle: <<paste here>>. Explain the economic loop, say whether it can be removed algebraically (interest on opening balance, tax before interest for sizing, average-balance IDC by closed form) and give the replacement formulas. Do not recommend iterative calculation unless the loop cannot be removed.
```
:::


**XIRR #NUM!**

::: {.prompt}
```text
XIRR returns #NUM!. Here are Val rows 47 to 50 for the first 6 columns and the sum of positive and negative flows: <<paste here>>. Check the first-column zero, the sign pattern and the date order, and give the fix.
```
:::


**DSCR below the target after sizing**

::: {.prompt}
```text
My sculpted DSCR is below the target <<target DSCR>> in some quarters. Here are Sculpt rows 20 to 23 and 34 to 38 and FinStat CFADS for those quarters: <<paste here>>. Tell me whether the sizing CFADS and the actual CFADS differ (tax before vs after interest), whether the gearing cap binds, and what to change.
```
:::


**Goal Seek will not converge**

::: {.prompt}
```text
Goal Seek on Sculpt!F32 by changing InpC gearing returns 'may not have found a solution'. Current gearing <<gearing>>, F32 = <<F32 value>>. Explain the bracket (gearing between 20% and 97%), the sign of F32, whether the facility input (InpC row 131) is stale, and propose a bisection to run manually.
```
:::


**Numbers differ from the course checkpoints**

::: {.prompt}
```text
My Base results differ from the course checkpoints (NPV 17,609.0 start model; blended IRR 43.03% PF model). Here are my sheet totals in column H: <<paste here>>. Walk the dependency chain from OpRev to Val and tell me the first sheet where a total differs and the probable cause (scenario name, unit, flag, sign, range).
```
:::


# Verification protocol {#sec-verify}

Three independent layers, each catching what the others cannot.

| Layer | What it proves | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Checks inside the workbook | Internal consistency: balance sheet, cash, income statement, sources = uses, debt repaid, deferred tax unwound. | Cover status and the FinStat, Time, Constr and Sculpt checks (B23). |
| 2. Independent replica | The formulas implement the stated logic: two different codebases agree to the precision of the checkpoints (6 decimals for the engine values). | Path D prompts; `node test/test_engine.js` reproduces 89 workbook reference values (all three scenarios, read from a full formula evaluation of the delivered workbooks; the same kind of list runs live on the app's Verify tab); `node test/test_options.js` runs 2,160 option combinations and requires finite results and a balancing balance sheet. |
| 3. Real Excel | No hidden dependency on a library: the file recalculates in Microsoft Excel to the same numbers, with zero error cells in all three scenarios. | The final workbooks (day-count correction, facility rule, automatic calculation mode) were recalculated in Microsoft Excel for Mac on 10 October 2026 for Base, Downside and Upside: project cost, debt, IRR, NPV and minimum DSCR equal the engine to 6 decimals, Cover reads ALL CHECKS PASSED and the Dashboard DSCR guard returns 0. Repeat this check in your own copy whenever you change anything. |

# Defects, corrections and retained conventions {#sec-defects}

Three groups: defects of the original file that the delivered model corrects (each a lesson in what the verify prompt must catch), defects of the earlier build of this model found in review and corrected, and conventions that are retained and documented.

## Defects of the original file (corrected)

| # | Defect | What was wrong | Correction | Block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Ghost formulas to column XFD | Seven sheets carried about 1.24 million formulas and formats beyond column CO; file 6.0 MB and recalculation took minutes. | Delete columns beyond CO; file 0.4 MB, recalculation in seconds. | B00 |
| D2 | Broken names and external links | LIVE_RESULTS, TRACK_ACTIVE and TRK_COMMENT pointed at deleted cells; 'unit' pointed at an external workbook; Track had sheet-level names to another file. | Rebuild the names; remove the links; extend the Time print area to CO. | B00, B12 |
| D3 | Typos and stray zeros | Scenario, arrival, Investment, Accounting, available, period, NPV of ...; stray zeros in Tax C28, C35, InpC row 45, InpS J74. | Correct the labels and clear the cells. | B01 |
| D4 | Short check and total ranges | Totals and checks stopped at columns BY, BV or CQ, so the last quarters were never tested; Time!H79 did not count the post-forecast flag. | Extend all total and check ranges to CO. | B10 |
| D5 | Incoherent scenarios | Upside was worse than Base (2% flat inflation) and Downside equalled Base; O&M sensitivity (InpC row 46) was not wired. | Base / Downside (fare -10%, O&M +10%) / Upside (fare +10%); row 46 live. | B01, B05 |
| D6 | Tax ignored interest | Tax row 26 (interest) was empty, so cash tax was overstated and deferred tax was stranded in retained earnings. | Link to Debt interest (and SHL interest in the PF model). | B06 |
| D7 | Empty placeholders | Debt row 42 and Equity row 22 (additional drawdown, share capital injection) were not fed from InpS rows 22 and 23 and did not reach the cash cascade and Val. | Pull them in and pass through FinStat rows 39 and 43 and Val rows 24 and 27. | B08, B09, B10, B11 |
| D8 | No lender ratios | No DSCR block in FinStat; no way to see cover. | Add FinStat rows 83 to 94 (debt service, DSCR, min, average, whole-life cover). | B10, B20 |
| D9 | New-function names | MINIFS written by a script without the _xlfn. prefix returns #NAME? in Excel. | Use _xlfn.MINIFS (found only by opening the file in real Excel). | B20 |
| D10 | Opening balance cosmetic | DSRA target before COD showed a value. | Multiply by (1 - Time!J58 + Time!J45) so it is zero before COD. | B18 |
| D16 | Manual calculation mode | Both workbooks were saved with calculation set to Manual (inherited from the original file), so after switching the scenario the results and checks stayed stale until F9 was pressed, contradicting the instruction that everything recalculates. | Saved in Automatic mode with full recalculation on load; B00 checks the setting. | B00 |
| D15 | Days in period one day short | Time row 30 = period end less period beginning (the first day of the month) gave 89 or 90 days for a quarter (a 361-day year) while Constr used true days, so interest, receivables and payables were slightly understated in every quarter. | Corrected: = end - beginning + 1. Effect against the original: Base senior debt 72,403 to 72,154, blended IRR 43.34% to 43.03%, start-model NPV 17,688 to 17,609. Confirmed in Microsoft Excel (10 Oct 2026) for all three scenarios; the app option 'original day count' reproduces the old numbers. | B02 |

## Defects of the earlier build, found in review (corrected)

| # | Defect | What was wrong | Correction | Block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D11 | Dashboard DSCR guard | The Dashboard DSCR row tested debt service for exactly zero; after maturity the value is float noise (-1.8e-12), so FY2032 to FY2041 showed DSCRs of about -1.7e16 and the DSCR chart was unusable. | =IF(ABS(debt service)>CHK_TOL, CFADS/debt service, 0). Verified in Excel: the row now shows 0 after maturity. | B23 |
| D12 | Facility set to DSCR capacity | When the 75% gearing cap binds (Upside, and any structure with a long tenor or low DSCR target) the facility was set to the DSCR capacity (89,663 for Upside), so upfront and commitment fees were charged on debt that could never be drawn. Upside project cost showed 101,912 instead of 101,402.9 and IRR 66.55% instead of 67.04% (original day count; after the day-count correction D15 the correct figures are 101,403.0 and 66.90%). | Facility = ROUND(MIN(capacity, gearing cap x project cost)); InpC row 131 for Upside is now 76,052. Workbook, replica and engine rebuilt; confirmed in Microsoft Excel for Mac on 10 October 2026 for the final build (with D15), all three scenarios. | B14, B16 |
| D13 | Cover status ignored the construction checks | The status formula contained a disabled term (+Constr!F55\*0), so construction errors could not turn the status red. | Status now also tests Constr!F55 and the sources-less-uses row 48 with CHK_TOL. | B23 |
| D14 | Hard-coded tolerance on Track | Track flags used a typed 0.001 instead of the named tolerance CHK_TOL. | Replaced by CHK_TOL. | B12 |

## Retained conventions (documented, not corrected)

| # | Convention | What it does | Effect and option | Block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Retained convention: sponsor funding dated at COD | Val dates all sponsor funding at COD although equity is paid in during construction, so the blended IRR (43.03% Base) and the NPV are both measured from COD and overstate the return; they cannot rank drawdown options. | Not changed in the workbook; the app also reports the IRR dated at the construction quarters (34.71% Base; equity first 32.03%). | B14, B19 |
| R2 | Retained convention: tax losses refunded | Negative taxable income produces a cash tax refund in the same quarter (4 quarters in Base, 11 in Downside). | Not changed; app option to carry losses forward (Downside minimum DSCR 2.34x to 2.25x). | B06 |

## Token reference for the interactive app

Tailored prompts replace tokens such as `{{rate}}` or `{{R.irr}}` with the values of the current run. Input tokens: `{{first}}`, `{{acq}}`, `{{nyrs}}`, `{{mpp}}`, `{{cpi0}}`, `{{cpiH}}`, `{{cpiO}}`, `{{capD}}`, `{{capI}}`, `{{fare}}`, `{{arDays}}`, `{{hFixed}}`, `{{hVar}}`, `{{omSens}}`, `{{omFixed}}`, `{{apDays}}`, `{{nca0}}`, `{{life}}`, `{{lifeCapex}}`, `{{gearing}}`, `{{profile}}`, `{{rate}}`, `{{dc}}`, `{{tdep}}`, `{{tax}}`, `{{valDate}}`, `{{yDays}}`, `{{req}}`, `{{constrN}}`, `{{hard}}`, `{{upfront}}`, `{{commit}}`, `{{facility}}`, `{{drawdown}}`, `{{eqCommit}}`, `{{tenor}}`, `{{dscr}}`, `{{gmax}}`, `{{dsraN}}`, `{{shlPct}}`, `{{shlRate}}`. Result tokens: `{{R.U}}`, `{{R.D}}`, `{{R.E}}`, `{{R.g}}`, `{{R.cap}}`, `{{R.binding}}`, `{{R.irr}}`, `{{R.npv}}`, `{{R.minDSCR}}`, `{{R.avgDSCR}}`, `{{R.llcr}}`, `{{R.plcr}}`, `{{R.maxDSRA}}`, `{{R.sumDiv}}`, `{{R.shlInt}}`, `{{R.shlPrin}}`, `{{R.idc}}`, `{{R.cfee}}`, `{{R.upfrontFee}}`, `{{R.hardTotal}}`, `{{R.sh0}}`, `{{R.sc0}}`. ## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CFADS | Cash flow available for debt service: operating cash flow less capex and tax. |
| COD | Commercial operation date; here 31 Dec 2021 (end of construction). |
| DSCR | CFADS divided by interest plus principal in the period. |
| LLCR / PLCR | Present value of CFADS over the loan life / project life divided by debt outstanding. |
| IDC | Interest during construction, capitalised into the project cost. |
| DSRA | Debt service reserve account holding the next N quarters of debt service. |
| SHL | Shareholder loan: subordinated sponsor funding that earns interest. |
| Sculpting | Shaping repayments so that DSCR is constant. |
| POS | Positive-number row; the next row flips the sign for the statements. |
| XIRR | Internal rate of return using actual dates (act/365). |
| FC | Financial close: the date the financing documents become effective and funds can be drawn. |
| CP | Condition precedent: an item that must be satisfied before a drawdown. |
| EoD | Event of default. |
| Lock-up | A test (for example DSCR below a threshold) that blocks distributions to sponsors. |
| MRA | Major-maintenance reserve account for lifecycle costs such as rolling-stock overhauls. |
| Step-in | A lender's right to take over or appoint a replacement operator or concessionaire to cure a default. |
| Direct agreement | A contract between the lenders and a project counterparty that protects the lenders' security. |
| Tail | The period between the final loan maturity and the end of the project or concession. |
| Lender's case | The conservative forecast (for example P90 traffic) on which the lenders size the debt. |
| P50 / P90 | Forecast values that are exceeded with 50% / 90% probability. |
| Restricted payment | A payment to sponsors (dividend, shareholder-loan interest or principal) that the credit agreement allows only if conditions are met. |
| R1C1 | A way of reading a formula by relative position (for example 'two columns left') instead of by cell address; two cells have the same R1C1 formula when they do the same thing relative to their position. |
| Gearing | Senior debt divided by total project cost (debt plus equity). |
| Tenor | The repayment period of the loan, here in quarters. |
| Goal Seek | An Excel tool that changes one input until another cell reaches a target value. |
| Flag | A row of 1s and 0s that switches a calculation on or off. |
| Anchor ($) | A dollar sign that stops a reference moving when a formula is filled across or down: $F11 keeps column F, J$5 keeps row 5. |
| Roll-forward | closing balance = opening balance + additions - reductions. |
| PIK | Payment in kind: interest added to the balance instead of paid in cash. |
